chunks: From him, from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad, from Yaʿqūb ibn Yazīd, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from a man, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
Every ghusl is preceded by wudu (ablution), except ghusl al-janābah.

key_terms.غُسْلٍ: ritual bath performed for a state of ritual purity
key_terms.غُسْلَ الْجَنَابَةِ: the ritual bath for major ritual impurity caused by janābah
key_terms.كُلُّ: every; expressing general applicability of the ruling
key_terms.وُضُوءٌ: ritual ablution performed before acts of worship such as salat (prayer)

ai.seo_question: Does every ghusl require wudu (ablution) beforehand in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling regarding ritual purity: wudu (ablution) is required before every ghusl except ghusl al-janābah. It is significant in fiqh discussions on whether certain ritual baths suffice on their own or require a prior wudu (ablution).
